memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'For two years now there has been famine in the land, and for the next five years there will be no plowing and reaping. But God sent me ahead of you to preserve for you a remnant on earth and to save your lives by a great deliverance.'" — Gen 45:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph now explains the scale of what is happening. Five more years of famine are coming. Without intervention, this family — the family through whom God had promised to bless all nations — would simply starve out of existence.

That word "remnant" is important. It appears again and again through Scripture: a preserved group, small and fragile, kept alive by God when everything around them is collapsing. God has always been in the business of preserving what looks like it cannot survive.

And notice the phrase "a great deliverance." Long before Israel walked out of Egypt through the Red Sea, God was already rescuing them — quietly, through the career of one faithful man. God's rescues do not always look dramatic at the time. Sometimes they look like a young man learning to manage grain.

Look at the timing too. God sent Joseph ahead. The provision was in place before the crisis arrived. Egypt's storehouses were being filled while Jacob's family still had food on the table and no idea anything was coming.

That is how God works for His people still. Whatever you are walking towards, He has already been there. In Christ, the greatest deliverance of all was prepared before the foundation of the world (1 Pet 1:20).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where has God provided for you before you even knew you would need it?
2. What "small" thing might God be using now to prepare for something you cannot see yet?
3. How does knowing God goes ahead of you change your view of the future?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You go ahead of me and prepare what I will need before I know I need it. Thank You for a salvation planned before the world began. Help me walk into tomorrow trusting that You are already there. Amen.
